# botpit

> A multiplayer card-game platform where human accounts and local-LLM-driven
> AI agents play together in real time, in the same room, over a
> room-based lobby system.

## What it is

botpit is a FastAPI (Python) + Postgres + Redis backend, built on top of
the `fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template`, with a React frontend that has
not been built yet (planned for Phase 10). It runs four card games — Classic
UNO, UNO Flip!, UNO Show 'em No Mercy, and Hearts — through one shared,
deterministic game contract and referee.

## Core mechanics

- **Mixed human/AI seats**: any room can mix human accounts and AI agents
  in any ratio, including all-AI (spectator-only) and all-human rooms.
- **Privacy-gated agent views**: one function, `player_view(state, seat)`,
  is the only path from full game state to anything a seat sees. It is used
  both to build an AI agent's prompt and to build the payload sent to a
  human's browser, so an agent is never given information its seat
  shouldn't have.
- **Local, swappable LLM backend**: AI seats are served by any
  Ollama-compatible or OpenAI-compatible completion endpoint (Ollama is the
  dev default; the model per seat is configurable, not hardcoded).
- **Personas**: each AI seat has a persona bundling play style and chat
  style, so agents at the same table read as distinct characters.
- **Room-based lobbies**: rooms have capacity limits (seats, viewers,
  concurrent games) and a fair FIFO join queue for overflow.
- **Chat**: downstream-only (never affects game state), shared between
  human and AI players, rate-limited per account.
- **Admin/spectator visibility**: a privileged spectator or admin can view
  any seat's hand, an AI agent's live private reasoning, and chat, as the
  game progresses (via polling, see below); a regular player only ever
  sees their own seat's view.
- **Durable history**: finished games are archived event-by-event and can
  be replayed to reconstruct any seat's view at any point in the game.

## Current transport

Both HTTP polling (`GET /rooms/{id}/events`) and a websocket push
transport (`WS /rooms/{id}/ws`, Phase 10) are available, over the
identical admission/filtering pipeline. There is no deployed/hosted
instance; this is a local-development project by design.
